what: Whether loading AR0 also loads ARCR and INDX on this part, under both PMST.NDX polarities
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2
why: SPRU056D contradicts itself: the LAR page and Table 4-3 say the 'C2x side effect happens when NDX is CLEAR, section 3.5's prose says when it is SET. The answer decides whether the resident's `lar ar0, @10` before each `cmpr eq` is what leaves a ring address in ARCR, which is the gate on the DSP's mailbox poll rate - docs/what-runs-and-what-blocks.md.
method: probe_transport --ndx, placed at 0x3000 with ATGLK2W (2144 word writes, verified byte-exact), started via IVT vector 8 and T0CON.INT at 0xff36. Sentinels ARCR=0xEEEE INDX=0xDDDD are rewritten before each load, so 'loaded' and 'untouched' are distinct.
findings: With NDX CLEAR the side effect HAPPENS: ARCR and INDX both take the value loaded into AR0.
With NDX SET it does NOT happen: both sentinels survive.
So the LAR page and Table 4-3 are right about the polarity and section 3.5's prose is wrong.

It is not limited to 'C2x instructions. `lar ar0, #4321` is the 'C5x long-immediate form and it loaded ARCR and INDX too, so the side effect is on loading AR0 at all, not on the encoding. The manual's 'C2x framing is misleading.
consequence: The mechanism behind the ARCR gate is real hardware behaviour, not a misreading. The resident clears NDX at 0x8012, so every `lar ar0, @10` on the live board loads ARCR and INDX from @10. What the harness must now explain is why implementing this breaks it (317 *0+/*0- sites corrupted, codec undriven) when the board runs fine - that is a harness bug or a missing constraint, not a reason to leave NDX unimplemented.
emulator: The harness never reads m_pmst.ndx and predicted sentinels under both polarities: 0030 EEEE DDDD EEEE DDDD EEEE DDDD 4321 0034 EEEE DDDD 1234. It is wrong for the NDX-clear half. Not changed by this run - see consequence above. emulator-frame.txt.
caveats: PMST reads 0x00b0/0x00b4 rather than 0x0030/0x0034: AVIS (bit 7) is set on the board and is not in the emulator's reset state. Bit 2 is what this run is about and it moved as intended.
AR0 in words 7 and 11 is what proves the loads executed at all; without it a sentinel could mean a skipped instruction.
Board left restored: vector 8 back to 8000:108F, T0CON back to 0x8021, AT answering. The image is still in RAM at 0x3000-0x40bf and is inert.
